fix.tests:
Fast tests on fix-altnum: node harness/selftest.js gives 945/945 (table failures 0). node harness/check.js gives "all page scripts ES5, ASCII, no forbidden calls"; no lookbehind is used.

The case file harness/cases/altnum.json (30 cases): the baseline (STEEL_SRC=base-src) passes 8 of 30, which are exactly the 8 must-not-change cases. The fixed tree passes 30 of 30. The baseline printout is saved in scratchpad/altnum/cases.base.txt.

Regression: 7585 questions, each run on the baseline and on my tree with node harness/batch.js --procs 2, then compared with harness/diff.js. The question files were every [{id,text}] file under A/** (beam, ccap, loads, look, tcap, tsel), B/clean-calc.json, B/clean-words.json, B/rough.json (3221 rough copies), B/cause/variants*.json and reg/probe-now.json. B/clean-all.json was left out because it duplicates clean-calc + clean-words. C/ was not used (it is a holdout).
- First set, 5616 questions: 2916 changed.
- Second set (files that appeared later), 1969 questions: 534 changed.

Every changed question was classified by scratchpad/altnum/classify.js, which requires all of the following:
- Same part count, kind, form, status, why, gate and read lines.
- The only write-line difference is an ANSWER (or ALSO FOUND / FOUND, BUT NOT) line split into the cut ANSWER line plus Check / For comparison lines.
- At most one number on the new ANSWER line, not counting shape names, the ^2 exponent or the label.
- Every number on the new lines was already on the old line.

Result: 3450 of 3450 are this kind of reformat. Newly right 0, stop->stop 0, other 0, WRONG 0, status changes 0.
